fields.businessMeaning: Name of the customer account
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: For an Individual account, this represents the customer’s name. For Corporate or Retail accounts, it represents the registered company or business name. Can be used in customer summaries, record identification and search.
fields.sensitiveClassification: PII for Individual; Internal/Business Data for Corporate and Retail
fields.importantRules: The meaning depends on RecordType.Name. The LLM must not assume every Account Name represents a person.

fields.businessMeaning: Formatted address associated with the account
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Can be used to describe the customer’s registered, residential or correspondence address.
fields.importantRules: It should not be interpreted as the address of the purchased property unless explicitly confirmed by another property-related field.

fields.businessMeaning: Number of opportunities associated with the account
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents how many sales or property opportunities are linked to the customer. Can be used to identify customers with single or multiple transactions.
fields.importantRules: This is a numeric count, not the number of properties currently owned. Cancelled, transferred or historical opportunities may be included depending on the Salesforce calculation logic.

fields.businessMeaning: Nationality of an individual customer
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Can be used for factual customer-profile summaries and aggregate demographic reporting.
fields.importantRules: Primarily applicable to Individual accounts. It should not be used for eligibility decisions, customer scoring, behavioural predictions or discriminatory profiling.

fields.businessMeaning: Age of an individual customer
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Can be used for factual summaries or approved age-group aggregation.
fields.importantRules: Primarily applicable to Individual accounts. It should not be used for discriminatory profiling or automated decision-making. Confirm whether this is a stored age or calculated from date of birth, because stored age can become outdated.

fields.businessMeaning: Identifies the business category of the account
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Determines whether the account represents an Individual, Corporate entity or Retail entity. This field controls how fields such as Account Name and Contact relationships should be interpreted.
fields.importantRules: Only Individual, Corporate and Retail records will be included. Other account record types should be excluded from the dataset.

fields.businessMeaning: Customer’s country of residence or registered billing country
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: For an Individual account, interpret this primarily as country of residence. For Corporate or Retail accounts, it may represent the registered or billing country of the business.
fields.sensitiveClassification: Personal Data for Individual; Business Data for Corporate/Retail
fields.importantRules: It is not necessarily the customer’s nationality and should not be treated as the location of a purchased property.

fields.businessMeaning: Name of the primary contact associated with a Corporate or Retail account
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Identifies the main person representing or communicating on behalf of the company or retail account. Can be included in relationship summaries.
fields.importantRules: Applicable mainly to Corporate and Retail accounts. The contact must not be interpreted as the owner of the company unless another field explicitly confirms ownership.

fields.businessMeaning: Full name of the person associated with the company or retail account
fields.semanticCategory: Treat as a person representing, working for or associated with the Account
fields.importantRules: Do not assume the person is the owner, authorized signatory or primary contact unless explicitly identified.

fields.businessMeaning: Job title or business designation of the contact
fields.semanticCategory: Describes the person’s role within the organization, such as Manager, Director or Finance Manager
fields.importantRules: Job titles may be manually entered and inconsistent. Use as descriptive information rather than a guaranteed authority level.

fields.businessMeaning: Mailing or correspondence address of the contact
fields.semanticCategory: Address used to contact the individual associated with the Corporate or Retail account
fields.importantRules: Do not automatically treat it as the company’s registered address, the Account address or the purchased property address.

Opportunity.objectDescription: Opportunity Object — LLM Data Dictionary Object-level definition An Opportunity represents a property-related transaction associated with a customer Account. Depending on its stage and status, it may represent an active booking, completed sale, cancelled transaction, transferred property transaction, or another sales lifecycle state. The LLM should not assume that every Opportunity represents a currently owned or successfully purchased property. Fields such as StageName, Order_Stattus__c, milestone status, and transfer-related business rules must be reviewed before describing the transaction. Opportunity field definitions

fields.businessMeaning: Unique Salesforce identifier of the Opportunity
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Used to uniquely identify, retrieve, join, or reference the Opportunity record
fields.importantRules: Should not normally appear in a customer-facing summary. Useful for system integration and record linking only.

fields.businessMeaning: Salesforce Opportunity name or transaction reference
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the business name or reference assigned to the property transaction
fields.importantRules: It may contain a booking number, customer name, unit reference, or generated naming format. It should not be interpreted without understanding the organization’s naming convention.

fields.businessMeaning: Current sales stage or final outcome of the Opportunity
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Indicates the commercial stage of the transaction, such as active, completed, won, lost, cancelled, or transferred
fields.importantRules: This is one of the primary fields used to determine whether the transaction is active, successful, unsuccessful, cancelled, or historical.

fields.businessMeaning: Name of the building, tower, phase, or property development linked to the Opportunity
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the specific building or development associated with the property transaction
fields.importantRules: It may be used as a property location or project grouping field. It should not automatically be treated as the community, city, postal address, or unit number.

fields.businessMeaning: Community or master development where the building is located
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the higher-level community containing the building, project, or development
fields.importantRules: Use this field for community-level grouping and summaries. It is broader than Building_Name__c.

fields.businessMeaning: Name of the salesperson responsible for the Opportunity
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Identifies the internal salesperson who manages or originated the transaction
fields.importantRules: It can be used for salesperson-level summaries and performance reporting. It should not automatically be interpreted as the current Opportunity Owner unless confirmed.

fields.businessMeaning: Standard Salesforce source through which the customer or transaction originated
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Indicates the original high-level source of the Opportunity, such as referral, website, event, walk-in, or campaign
fields.importantRules: Values may be broad or manually selected. It should be distinguished from the more detailed lead channel field.

fields.businessMeaning: Detailed business or sales channel associated with the Opportunity
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Provides a more specific classification of how the customer or booking was generated
fields.importantRules: May overlap with LeadSource, but usually provides a more detailed or organization-specific channel classification.

fields.businessMeaning: Standard gross amount associated with the Opportunity
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the standard Salesforce Opportunity amount, typically the gross sales or transaction value
fields.importantRules: Currency must be identified from Salesforce currency settings. It should not automatically be considered the final payable or net amount.

fields.businessMeaning: Expected or actual commercial closing date of the Opportunity
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the expected close date for an open Opportunity or the closing date used when the transaction was completed
fields.importantRules: It may be forecast-oriented for open Opportunities. Do not always interpret it as the actual property booking date or order date.

fields.businessMeaning: Current stage or status of the mortgage process
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Indicates the customer’s current mortgage or financing progress for the property transaction
fields.importantRules: It should not be interpreted as final mortgage approval unless the field value explicitly indicates approval. Blank may mean not applicable, cash purchase, or not yet updated.

fields.businessMeaning: Date on which the property was reserved or booked
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the actual date on which the customer booked or reserved the property
fields.importantRules: Usually more appropriate than CloseDate for booking-trend analysis. It does not necessarily mean the transaction was later completed.

fields.businessMeaning: Current operational, construction, handover, or customer journey milestone
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the latest known milestone reached in the property lifecycle or handover process
fields.importantRules: This may describe construction, notification, orientation, appointment, key release, or handover progress. It is not the same as the Opportunity sales stage.

fields.businessMeaning: Salesforce lookup identifier for the agency associated with the Opportunity
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Used to link the Opportunity with an external real-estate agency record
fields.importantRules: The raw lookup ID should be used for relationships and system joins. It should not normally be displayed in summaries.

fields.businessMeaning: Name of the external agency associated with the Opportunity
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Identifies the agency that introduced, managed, or supported the transaction
fields.importantRules: Use the related name for readable summaries. The agency’s exact responsibility may depend on the business process.

fields.businessMeaning: Salesforce lookup identifier for the individual agent associated with the Opportunity
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Links the Opportunity to an individual broker or agent record
fields.importantRules: The raw lookup ID should not normally appear in natural-language summaries.

fields.businessMeaning: Name of the broker or agent associated with the transaction
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Identifies the individual external agent or broker linked to the Opportunity
fields.importantRules: Do not assume the agent is employed directly by the organization. They may be associated with the selected agency.

fields.businessMeaning: Sales room, branch, office, kiosk, or sales location associated with the booking
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the physical or operational sales location from which the transaction was handled
fields.importantRules: It should not be interpreted as the property location. A property can be sold through a sales room located elsewhere.

fields.businessMeaning: Current status of the sales order related to the Opportunity
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Indicates the operational status of the associated order, such as active, processed, cancelled, transferred, or completed
fields.importantRules: The API name contains Stattus, which appears to be an intentional Salesforce field spelling. The exact meaning depends on the configured picklist values.

fields.businessMeaning: Date on which the sales order was created, confirmed, or processed
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the business date associated with the formal sales order
fields.importantRules: It may differ from the property booking date and Opportunity close date. The exact business trigger for setting this date should be documented.

fields.businessMeaning: Net value of the transaction after applicable adjustments
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the net financial amount after discounts, adjustments, exclusions, or other business calculations
fields.importantRules: The calculation should be documented. It should not automatically be treated as the amount paid, amount outstanding, or recognized revenue.

Opportunity_Property__c.objectDescription: Opportunity Property Object — LLM Data Dictionary Opportunity_Property__c Object-level business definition Opportunity_Property__c represents the property-related transaction details associated with an Opportunity. It is not the actual inventory master record. The object acts as a transaction-detail or association record containing information such as: The property reference linked to the transaction Order status and order date Property area details Selling and net transaction values VAT-inclusive values Receipt, installment, and invoice clearance progress Construction status Parking and garage details The relationship should be interpreted as: → Opportunity Property → Associated property or inventory reference The LLM should understand: The Account represents the customer. The Opportunity represents the commercial transaction. The Opportunity Property represents the property-related details of that transaction. The actual inventory master may exist in another Salesforce object. The LLM must not describe Opportunity_Property__c itself as the inventory unit. Field definitions

fields.businessMeaning: Property or inventory location reference associated with the transaction
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Identifies the property associated with the Opportunity using a structured internal reference code
fields.importantRules: This is a reference value. It does not mean the Opportunity Property record itself is the inventory master. Do not decode individual code segments without an approved mapping.

fields.businessMeaning: Current order status of the property transaction
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Indicates the operational status of the order for the property associated with the Opportunity
fields.importantRules: Has the same business meaning as the order-status field on Opportunity. If the values differ, flag the discrepancy rather than selecting one silently.

fields.businessMeaning: Date associated with the formal property order
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the date on which the order was created, confirmed, or processed for the property transaction
fields.importantRules: Has the same business meaning as the order-date field on Opportunity. It is different from booking date and Opportunity close date.

fields.businessMeaning: Total land or plot area associated with the property
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the size of the land or plot connected with the property transaction
fields.importantRules: Mainly applicable to villas, townhouses, plots, or landed properties. It may be blank or not applicable for apartments and some retail units.

fields.businessMeaning: Overall recorded area of the property associated with the transaction
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the total area recorded for the property
fields.importantRules: It may include or exclude terrace, garage, or other component areas depending on the business calculation.

fields.businessMeaning: Area considered for sale or lease calculations
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the commercially saleable or leasable area associated with the property transaction
fields.importantRules: It may differ from total area, plot area, built-up area, or regulatory area.

fields.businessMeaning: Selling price after applicable commercial adjustments
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the adjusted selling price after discounts, premiums, or other configured commercial calculations
fields.importantRules: It should not automatically be treated as the amount paid, outstanding balance, or VAT-inclusive amount.

fields.businessMeaning: Base or gross selling price associated with the property transaction
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the primary selling price before applicable net adjustments
fields.importantRules: The exact inclusion of discounts, fees, or VAT depends on the business calculation.

fields.businessMeaning: Net financial amount recorded for the property transaction
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the net transaction value after applicable adjustments
fields.importantRules: It may differ from Net_Selling_Price__c. The two fields should not be treated as identical unless the business formula confirms this.

fields.businessMeaning: Net transaction amount after VAT is included
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the net amount inclusive of VAT
fields.importantRules: It does not represent VAT amount alone, amount paid, outstanding balance, or recognized revenue.

fields.businessMeaning: Percentage of the expected receipt value that has cleared
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Indicates the percentage of receipt value successfully cleared
fields.importantRules: This is a percentage field, not a currency amount.

fields.businessMeaning: Monetary amount represented by cleared receipts
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the actual currency value of cleared receipts
fields.importantRules: Do not confuse it with receipt-clearance percentage or total amount paid across all payment sources.

fields.businessMeaning: Percentage of scheduled installments that have cleared
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Indicates installment-clearance progress as a percentage
fields.importantRules: This is a percentage field. It is not the number of installments or the monetary amount of cleared installments.

fields.businessMeaning: Percentage of invoiced value that has cleared
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Indicates the percentage of the invoiced amount successfully cleared
fields.importantRules: Despite “Amount” appearing in the API name, this is a percentage field and should be displayed as such.

fields.businessMeaning: Area allocated to a terrace, balcony, or external terrace space
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the separately recorded terrace area associated with the property
fields.importantRules: It may or may not already be included in total area. Do not add it to total area unless an approved calculation is provided.

fields.businessMeaning: Physical area allocated to a garage
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the separately recorded garage area associated with the property
fields.importantRules: Garage area is different from parking count. One garage may contain one or more parking spaces.

fields.businessMeaning: Current physical construction or completion status of the property
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the current construction stage of the property associated with the transaction
fields.importantRules: It is separate from Opportunity sales stage, order status, and handover milestone status.

fields.businessMeaning: Number of parking spaces allocated to the property
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the quantity of parking spaces associated with the property
fields.importantRules: This is a count, not an area. A blank value does not necessarily mean zero parking spaces.

Property_Inventory__c.objectDescription: Property Inventory Object — LLM Data Dictionary Property_Inventory__c Object-level business definition Property_Inventory__c represents the actual physical property inventory unit managed within Salesforce. Each record may represent a specific: Other saleable or leasable property This object is the authoritative inventory-level source for understanding: The unit’s current availability or occupancy status Whether the unit is intended for sale, rent, or is blocked The physical unit type and usage Unit location, view, and position Current and strategic pricing Price per square foot Estimated completion date DLD-recorded area The relationship may be interpreted as: Property Inventory → Actual physical property or unit → Customer transaction Opportunity Property → Property-related transaction details and association The LLM should use Property_Inventory__c when answering questions about: Available inventory Reserved or booked units Blocked inventory Rental inventory Unit types and usage Inventory pricing Inventory completion timelines Field definitions

fields.businessMeaning: View or outlook associated with the unit
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Describes what the unit overlooks or faces, such as park, pool, road, community, garden, or another feature
fields.importantRules: Values may be descriptive and inconsistent. Do not interpret a view as a guaranteed permanent feature unless contractually confirmed.

fields.businessMeaning: Physical position or orientation of the unit within the building, project, row, or development
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Describes where the unit is positioned, such as corner, middle, end, internal, external, front, rear, or another configured position
fields.importantRules: It is not necessarily a geographic direction unless the configured value explicitly represents one.

fields.businessMeaning: Selling price calculated per square foot of area
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the unit’s sales price rate per square foot
fields.importantRules: The area basis used in the calculation must be known. It may use saleable area, DLD area, total area, or another configured area.

fields.businessMeaning: Base price of the inventory unit
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Despite the API name, this field should be interpreted as the unit’s base price
fields.importantRules: The word “Penalty” in the API name is misleading. The LLM must not describe it as a customer penalty, fine, overdue charge, or cancellation fee.

fields.businessMeaning: Strategic or commercially targeted selling price assigned to the inventory
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents a strategically determined sales price based on commercial planning, positioning, demand, or management decisions
fields.importantRules: It may differ from base price and current selling price. Do not assume it is the final contractual value.

fields.businessMeaning: Current or standard selling price of the inventory unit
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the current selling price recorded against the inventory unit
fields.importantRules: It should not automatically be treated as the final sold value or amount paid by a customer.

fields.businessMeaning: Net selling price after applicable adjustments
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the selling price after configured discounts, premiums, adjustments, or other commercial calculations
fields.importantRules: It may differ from the final transaction value recorded on the Opportunity or Opportunity Property.

fields.businessMeaning: Detailed configuration, layout, bedroom type, model, or unit category
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Describes the detailed configuration of the inventory, such as studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom, three-bedroom, or another configured unit model
fields.importantRules: This should remain separate from Type__c, which represents the broader property form such as Villa.

fields.businessMeaning: Building, project, phase, cluster, or inventory location associated with the unit
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Identifies where the actual inventory unit is located within the property portfolio
fields.importantRules: It may represent a building or project-level name rather than a complete address.

fields.businessMeaning: Estimated date on which construction or development of the inventory unit is expected to be completed
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Indicates the expected construction-completion date for the unit
fields.importantRules: This is an estimate and may change. It should not be presented as an actual completion, handover, or key-release date.

fields.businessMeaning: Intended functional use of the inventory
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Identifies whether the unit is residential, commercial, retail, mixed-use, or another usage category
fields.importantRules: This describes intended usage, not current sales or leasing status.

fields.businessMeaning: Commercial inventory classification indicating whether the unit is for sale, rent, or blocked
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Indicates how the unit is currently classified for commercial handling
fields.importantRules: Based on the provided values, this is not the physical property type. It should not be used to identify whether the unit is a villa, apartment, or townhouse.

fields.businessMeaning: Current operational availability or occupancy status of the inventory unit
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Indicates the unit’s current position in the inventory lifecycle, such as available, reserved, booked, sold, blocked, leased, or online blocked
fields.importantRules: This should be the main field for current inventory-status summaries and counts.

fields.businessMeaning: Broad physical property form
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Identifies the high-level property type, such as Villa
fields.importantRules: This is different from Type_of_Unit__c, which may describe the detailed layout or configuration.

fields.businessMeaning: Total property area recorded with or recognized by DLD
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Represents the DLD Total Area for the inventory unit
fields.importantRules: The API name is generic and does not explain the meaning. The LLM should use the business label “DLD Total Area.” The unit of measurement must be confirmed before display.

Case.objectDescription: Case Object — LLM Data Dictionary Object-level business definition The Case object represents a customer service request, operational request, enquiry, complaint, registration, approval request, or another service-related interaction. Cases may be associated with: A corporate or retail entity A property or unit An internal service process For LLM summarization and category analysis, only parent Cases should be included. Child Cases should be excluded because they may represent internal workflow steps, departmental tasks, approvals, or sub-processes created from the original customer request. Parent Case filtering rule The dataset should include only records where Case_Type__c indicates that the Case is a parent Case. Conceptual filter: Case_Type__c = "Parent Case" The exact stored picklist value should be used from Salesforce. The LLM should not count parent and child Cases together, because this may duplicate a single customer request across multiple operational steps. Field definitions

fields.businessMeaning: Unique customer service Case reference generated by Salesforce
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Used to uniquely identify and reference the Case
fields.importantRules: Suitable for retrieval and traceability. It should not normally be included in aggregated summaries unless a detailed case list is requested.

fields.businessMeaning: Short description or business category of the customer request
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Describes the nature of the Case and may be used to classify or summarize the service request
fields.importantRules: For most Case types, this is one of the primary fields used for category-based reporting. For Contact Centre records, it should not be used as the main categorization field.

fields.businessMeaning: Current operational status of the Case
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Indicates whether the Case is new, open, in progress, pending, resolved, closed, or in another configured state
fields.importantRules: Status values should be interpreted using the organization’s Case-status definitions. A closed status does not necessarily mean the request was successfully completed unless the process confirms this.

fields.businessMeaning: Salesforce lookup to the Account associated with the Case
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Connects the Case to the individual, corporate, or retail customer account
fields.importantRules: Use for joins and customer-level summaries. The raw Salesforce ID should not normally appear in natural-language output.

fields.businessMeaning: Salesforce lookup to the Contact associated with the Case
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Identifies the person who raised, represents, or is associated with the Case
fields.importantRules: A Contact may be the requester, representative, tenant, employee, or another associated person. Do not automatically interpret the Contact as the Account owner.

fields.businessMeaning: Opportunity associated with the Case
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Links the service request to a specific property transaction or Opportunity
fields.importantRules: The API name contains the spelling Opporutniy. Preserve the actual API name in queries. The relationship may be stored as a lookup or another reference type.

fields.businessMeaning: Administrative or configured eService name associated with the Case
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Identifies the formal eService or administrative service type under which the Case was created
fields.importantRules: For most non-Contact-Centre Cases, this can be used as a primary service-category field. It should not be relied on for Contact Centre categorization where the value may be absent, broad, or unsuitable.

fields.businessMeaning: Salesforce Case record type
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Identifies the Case process, department, channel, or service framework
fields.importantRules: For Contact Centre records, Record Type should be used as the primary categorization basis where Subject and eService name are not suitable.

fields.businessMeaning: Channel through which the Case was created
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Identifies whether the request originated through phone, email, web, portal, internal entry, contact centre, or another configured channel
fields.importantRules: Origin describes how the Case was received, not what the customer requested. It should not be used as the service category.

fields.businessMeaning: Indicates whether the Case is a parent Case or child Case
fields.llmInterpretationAndUsage: Used to separate the original customer request from operational child Cases
fields.importantRules: Only parent Cases should be included in customer-request counts and category summaries.
